messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: elevated packet loss and intermittent BGP route churn observed for upstream ASN 64599 in eu-central interconnects. Multiple customer flows showing increased tail latency and 5xx rates. Paging @alex_oncall and @kira_net. Please triage.

alex_oncall: seeing the alert, joining. quick question — is this confined to eu-central or cross-region?

kira_net: initial telemetry shows high packet loss from our ashburn->eus transit path and duplicated but misordered updates into eu-central peer fabric. Looks like prefix flapping across two upstream providers.

leah_sre: @kira_net can you post the BGP dump and recent RIB diffs? I want to confirm whether our prepends/communities changed.

kira_net: pastebin: recent bgp diff (trimmed):
```
+ 203.0.113.0/24 via 192.0.2.1 as-path: ... 64599 2914
- 203.0.113.0/24 via 198.51.100.2 as-path: ... 64512 64599
+ 203.0.113.0/24 via 192.0.2.3 as-path: ... 64599
```
We got simultaneous withdraws + re-advertisements. ASN 64599 origin oscillating, likely provider-side.

alex_oncall: checking datadog dashboards — inference p95 token latency up 3x for customers in eu-central and some cross-region calls failing with connection resets. No internal config changes in the last 6 hours.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: No deploys in the last 6 hours.

leah_sre: sounds like upstream peering churn. Move to mitigation mode: 1) shift critical model traffic to dedicated fallback PoP in eu-west using route preference; 2) open ticket with vendor NOC + ask for immediate mitigation; 3) enable more aggressive BFD timers on affected sessions if safe.

kira_net: agreed. I'll adjust outbound locality preferences and clamp preference for eu-west for routing groups that carry inference traffic. Doing a staged rollout — will change a single route-target and observe.

kira_net: running command:
```
set policy route-prefer id=inf-prod prefer=eu-west priority=50
```
Applying to 1/3 route groups now.

vendor-noc: (vendor-noc) Acknowledged ticket TN-88421 raised to provider ASN 64599. They report a partial hardware failure on one of their core route reflectors and are rehoming sessions. Engineer on call is engaged. ETA unknown.

alex_oncall: good to have them engaged. Leah — can we update customers via status page about degraded performance in eu-central? I can draft a short blurb.

leah_sre: please do. Keep message conservative: degraded tail latency and intermittent 5xx in eu-central, mitigation in progress, no data loss.

alex_oncall: Draft for status page: "We are investigating increased latency and intermittent errors for customers primarily in EU-Central caused by upstream peering instability. Engineers are mitigating by shifting traffic and working with the transit provider. We will provide updates every 30 minutes." Anyone object?

kira_net: fine. post it.

alex_oncall: posted to status.redwood.com — incident created: RINF-2026-03-15-01.

leah_sre: after the first route preference change p95 latency in eu-central dropped ~30% but still elevated. Packet loss on ashburn->eu-central path reduced after we shifted second group.

kira_net: after 2/3 staged changes: paths now prefer eu-west for high-throughput inference routes. Immediate customer impact reduced for most customers, but some long-lived connections still experience resets (need connection-level retries).

ops-bot: paging checklist: mitigation applied, vendor engaged, status published, notify comms.

vendor-noc: Provider update: core rR failed NIC, they are toggling rR peers and rebalancing iBGP sessions. They recommend we prepending to avoid a specific transit fabric while they heal.

kira_net: I'll add a temp prepend for the problem AS path to steer away:
```
set policy as-path-prepend prefix=203.0.113.0/24 prepend=2 target=upstream-64599 temp-duration=60m
```
Applying now.

alex_oncall: Good. Keep an eye on connection timeouts. Also bringing @infra-sre in for potential autoscaler throttle if RPCs spike.

infra-sre: on it. Will pause noncritical autoscaling events and tune queue timeouts to reduce thundering herd.

leah_sre: timeline note: 2287654321 initial alert; 2287654400 vendor engaged; 2287654460 first route pref change; 2287654620 as-path prepend applied; 2287654800 significant reduction in error rates; 2287654959 handing over to night shift for follow-up.

alex_oncall: handing off to @kira_net for overnight watch. I'll write a short handoff message and required next steps.

kira_net: accepted. Next steps in handoff: 1) monitor vendor ticket updates; 2) revert temp prepends after provider confirms rR stability; 3) watch for increased egress costs due to reroute; 4) coordinate any customer-impacting changes with leah_sre before action.

leah_sre: I'll run an eval set against a small traffic shard in eu-central to validate correctness once provider confirms. Also schedule follow-up postmortem with network and SRE teams.

alex_oncall: handoff summary posted in the thread. Adding final note: no evidence of data corruption, only transient errors and latency. Thanks team — @kira_net you'll be primary until cleared.

vendor-noc: Provider updated: route reflector NIC replaced, iBGP sessions stable. Please confirm after you revert prepends.

kira_net: rolling back prepends now and reverting route preferences back to original. Post-rollback p95 latency stable and error rate at baseline.

leah_sre: marking incident as mitigated, moving to monitor state. Will capture RCA draft tonight.

ops-bot: Incident RINF-2026-03-15-01 moved to MONITORING.

alex_oncall: Thanks everyone. Handoff complete.
